-157.83300,21.29980.name: Pacific In Vitro Fertilization Institute
-157.83300,21.29980.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Thomas S. Kosasa, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-97.03063,47.92521.name: University of North Dakota
-97.03063,47.92521.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.18882,51.48625.name: Dr Kat Fertility
-0.18882,51.48625.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to King’s Fertility. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-89.25979,48.41987.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2022. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.35600,39.47500.name: IVIRMA Global
-0.35600,39.47500.state: Valencia — Plaza de la Policia Local 3
-0.35600,39.47500.desc: One of the largest fertility groups in the world, operating clinics across dozens of countries and running its own research institute. Fertility care is consolidating into international chains, so treatment protocols, add-on offerings and pricing are increasingly set at group level rather than by the clinic a patient walks into.

-3.20000,55.86500.name: Roslin Institute
-3.20000,55.86500.desc: Where Dolly the sheep was cloned in 1996, and still a centre for farm animal genetics and editing — the PRRS-resistant pig approved in the United States in 2025 came out of work done here. Dolly is the reason the public argument about animal biotechnology has the shape it does: cloning a mammal from an adult cell was announced as a technical result and received as a question about human cloning, and the regulatory reflexes formed in that year still govern editing done for entirely different reasons.

-108.98000,25.69000.name: GM maize found growing in Mexico despite the planting prohibition
-108.98000,25.69000.type: Maize, unapproved cultivation in a centre of origin
-108.98000,25.69000.size: Detected in commercial fields and in tortilla samples
-108.98000,25.69000.desc: GM maize found growing in Mexico despite the planting prohibition, in the north where seed crosses the border with trade. A prohibition on planting does not stop seed arriving.

39.10000,22.31000.name: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology — desert agriculture
39.10000,22.31000.desc: Research on crops for saline water and extreme heat, funded at a scale few public institutions match. Salinity and heat tolerance affect an enormous and growing area of farmland worldwide and attract a fraction of the investment that herbicide tolerance does, so where this work is funded at all is worth knowing.

-77.15200,39.08400.name: Adaptive Phage Therapeutics (BiomX)
-77.15200,39.08400.desc: Supplies bacteriophages, including engineered ones, matched to a patient’s specific infection when antibiotics have failed. Treatment is often given under compassionate-use rules rather than an approval, so the therapy reaches people through the exception rather than the process — which means the record of who received what is held by hospitals rather than by a regulator.

36.82190,-1.29210.name: African Agricultural Technology Foundation (AATF)
36.82190,-1.29210.desc: The body that holds the licences. Bayer, formerly Monsanto, granted AATF a non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free licence to two insect-resistance traits and a drought-tolerance trait, with the right to sub-license African seed companies to sell the resulting hybrids under their own brands, provided no royalty is charged onward. That is the legal architecture behind TELA maize in Ethiopia, Kenya, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania and Uganda, and behind pod-borer resistant cowpea. Registered in Kenya and as a charity in England and Wales, funded principally by the Gates Foundation and USAID. Royalty-free is not the same as unowned: each party keeps the intellectual property it brought, so the traits remain Bayer's and the licence is a permission that was granted and can be bounded.

36.82190,-1.29210.name: Kenyan GMO petitions (consolidated)
36.82190,-1.29210.state: Nairobi — High Court of Kenya and the Environment and Land Court
36.82190,-1.29210.desc: Kenya lifted a ten-year ban on engineered organisms in 2022 and was immediately taken to court. The petitions raised freedom of conscience, the right of access to information, the right to food of acceptable quality, and whether the regulations in place were sufficient. The Environment and Land Court ruled in 2023 and the consolidated petitions were dismissed in 2024. The case belongs here for two reasons and neither is the outcome. It shows what a challenge to a lifting looks like as opposed to a challenge to an approval, and it shows the cost of pendency working the other way: four Bt cotton varieties recommended for release, and six more through national performance and distinctness testing, sat unreleased while it ran. A case that is lost can still have suspended a release for two years, and a case that is won can be undone by the same delay in reverse.

-89.33900,43.24500.name: ABS Global
-89.33900,43.24500.state: DeForest, Wisconsin — a Genus plc company
-89.33900,43.24500.desc: A bovine genetics company founded in 1941, operating in seventy countries, and the arm through which its listed parent sells sex-sorted semen under the Sexcel brand. Sorting sperm by sex is not gene editing, and this facet should say so plainly — but it is the same industrial decision at one remove: which part of a herd passes on its genetics, and whether the calf is born male or female, chosen at the point of insemination. Sexed doses retail at roughly three to five times the price of conventional ones. The company also owns a Brazilian bovine IVF business outright. A reader following engineered livestock will find the editing companies elsewhere on this map; the firms that already decide which animals reproduce are these, and they were here first.
